plan.title: Alan Turing: The Man Who Taught Machines to Think
plan.description: A quick look at Alan Turing, the British mathematician who helped break wartime codes and asked whether machines can think. His ideas still shape every computer we use.

beats.narration: He helped win a world war, and then his country punished him. Alan Turing was a British mathematician who changed history.

props.text: He helped win a war. Then he was punished.

beats.narration: During the Second World War, he worked to break secret enemy codes. His work helped the Allies read messages that were meant to stay hidden.
He also imagined a universal machine that could follow any set of instructions. That idea became the blueprint for the modern computer, and he asked whether machines could think.
Yet he was treated cruelly for who he was. Today we honor him, and every device you touch carries his ideas.

props.alt: Modern devices that carry Turing's ideas
